Table 1 reports results from intention-to-treat effects of the graduation program on indexed family outcomes. Columns (1) to (3) report results from Ethiopia, and Columns (4) to (6) from India, as presented in Banerjee et al. 2021. ... Reported q-values are sharpened using the false discovery rate procedure detailed in Anderson (2008). They reflect a correction for 10 family outcomes in Ethiopia, and 9 family outcomes in India.
context_needed: Barker, Karlan, Udry and Wright: long-run follow-up of the graduation pilot run by the Relief Society of Tigray (REST) in Tigray, Ethiopia (PDF page 3): very poor households eligible for the PSNP, one programme arm against control by lottery. The note gives the estimand (intention-to-treat) and the units (indices standardised to the baseline, or to the endline-1 control group when baseline data are missing; asset ownership, consumption and time use are aggregated and rescaled). Columns (1)-(3) are this study's Ethiopia rounds, two, three and seven years after the asset transfer. Columns (4)-(6) are India (West Bengal) results 'as presented in Banerjee et al. 2021', i.e. a different programme and study.

not_stored.reason: multiple-testing adjusted inference (sharpened FDR q-values, Anderson 2008, over 10 family outcomes in Ethiopia). A test statistic, not an effect. Recorded here so the reader knows the estimates above them are the effects.

not_stored.cell: Columns (4)-(6) India: 1.5, 3 and 7 years (all estimates, SEs, q-values, means)
not_stored.reason: findings the paper reports from another study (Banerjee, Duflo and Sharma 2021, West Bengal), shown only for comparison. Never stored from this paper.

rule: When a q-value (or FWER-adjusted p-value) row sits under each estimate and SE, store the estimate and SE and skip the q-value line like any p-value, together with the control and baseline means. Columns the note attributes to another study ('as presented in Banerjee et al. 2021') are never stored, even when they share the table. A result the paper reprints from an earlier round of the same experiment is stored and linked to the first report (linked_to). Results from a different study (here the India columns) are never stored.

resolved_questions.question: Columns (1) and (2), the Ethiopia two- and three-year effects, belong to the same experiment whose two- and three-year results were first published in Banerjee et al. (2015), which is also among the 49 documents (893989dfb5e9). This paper re-presents them under its own index definitions. Are they stored here as this study's own estimates (as done here), or deduplicated against Banerjee et al. (2015)?
resolved_questions.resolution: Decided by Lucas, 22 Nov 2026: store reprints of the same experiment's results in both papers, linked.
